## The Two Worlds of LLMs

### A Working Taxonomy

- **Frontier / proprietary models**: weights never leave the lab; access via API only
- **Open-weight models**: weights downloadable; run them anywhere
- The capability gap has narrowed dramatically — the choice is now an engineering decision, not a foregone conclusion
- Most real organizations end up with a **portfolio** of both

## Frontier Labs: The Landscape

### API-Only Model Families

- **OpenAI**: GPT-5 family; reasoning-focused variants; realtime and multimodal endpoints
- **Anthropic**: Claude 4.x family (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku tiers)
- **Google DeepMind**: Gemini 2.5 / Gemini 3 family; deep Workspace/Cloud integration
- Common traits: strongest raw capability, managed safety, rapid iteration, per-token pricing

## Open-Weight Families

### Downloadable Model Lines

- **Meta Llama 4**: mixture-of-experts, multimodal, community license
- **DeepSeek V3 / R1**: strong MoE base + open reasoning model, permissive licensing
- **Qwen 3** (Alibaba): broad size range, strong multilingual and coding variants
- **Mistral**: efficient dense and MoE models, mix of Apache-2.0 and research licenses
- **gpt-oss** (OpenAI): open-weight reasoning models under Apache-2.0
- Hugging Face Hub is the de facto distribution channel

## Open Weights ≠ Open Source

### The Distinction That Matters

- **Open weights**: you get the trained parameters — enough to run, fine-tune, and deploy
- **Open source (strict sense)**: also training code, data recipe, and an OSI-approved license
- Most "open" LLMs release weights + inference code, **not** training data
- The OSI's Open Source AI Definition formalizes what qualifies
- Why it matters: reproducibility, auditability, and what your license actually permits

## Licenses: Apache-2.0 vs. Community Licenses

### Read Before You Ship

- **Apache-2.0 / MIT** (e.g., many Mistral and Qwen releases, gpt-oss): permissive, commercial use, few strings
- **Community licenses** (e.g., Llama): custom terms — acceptable-use policies, redistribution rules, thresholds for very large deployments
- **Research-only licenses**: no commercial use at all
- Derivative rules: what applies to your fine-tunes and distilled models?
- Legal review is part of model selection, not an afterthought

## What "Frontier" Buys You

### Strengths of Proprietary APIs

- Highest capability on the hardest tasks (long-horizon reasoning, agentic coding)
- Zero infrastructure: no GPUs to run, patch, or scale
- Fast access to new capabilities (multimodal, computer use, long context)
- Managed safety systems and abuse monitoring
- Enterprise contracts: SLAs, data-processing agreements

## What Open Weights Buy You

### Strengths of Self-Managed Models

- **Control**: pin a version forever; no silent model updates or deprecations
- **Privacy**: data never leaves your VPC or datacenter
- **Customization**: full fine-tuning freedom (Week 11)
- **Cost at scale**: high sustained volume can undercut per-token pricing
- **Latency**: co-locate the model with your application
- **No vendor lock-in**: portable across clouds and serving stacks

## Model Selection Criteria

### A Practical Checklist

::: {.incremental}
- **Task fit**: measured quality on *your* evals — not leaderboard rank
- **Modality & context**: text/vision/audio, context window needs
- **Latency budget**: interactive vs. batch
- **Cost model**: per-token API vs. amortized GPU spend
- **Data constraints**: residency, confidentiality, compliance regimes
- **License**: permitted use, redistribution, derivatives
- **Ecosystem**: tooling, serving support, community fine-tunes
:::

## Benchmarks and Their Limits

### Evaluate for Yourself

- Public leaderboards (e.g., LMArena, Hugging Face leaderboards) are a starting point, not a decision
- **Contamination**: benchmark data leaks into training sets
- **Saturation**: many classic benchmarks no longer discriminate at the top
- **Goodhart's law**: labs optimize for what is measured
- The Week 6 lesson applies: build a private eval set from your own traffic

## Self-Host vs. Third-Party API

### The Core Tradeoff Matrix

| Dimension | 3P API (frontier) | Self-hosted (open weights) |
|-----------|-------------------|----------------------------|
| Capability ceiling | Highest | High and rising |
| Data privacy | Provider-dependent | Full control |
| Ops burden | None | GPUs, serving, upgrades |
| Cost profile | Per-token, scales linearly | Fixed + marginal, wins at volume |
| Version control | Provider-controlled | You pin the weights |
| Time to start | Minutes | Days-weeks |

## Self-Hosting: The Serving Stack

### What Running Your Own Model Requires

- **Inference engines**: vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM (from the inference week)
- **Quantization**: FP8/INT4 to fit models on available GPUs
- **Autoscaling and batching**: utilization determines real cost
- **Middle path — managed open weights**: Amazon Bedrock, Azure AI Foundry, Together, Fireworks serve open models as APIs
- You can adopt open weights without owning GPUs

## Total Cost of Ownership

### Beyond the Sticker Price

- API costs: input/output tokens, cache discounts, batch tiers
- Self-host costs: GPU hours, engineering time, idle capacity, on-call
- Break-even depends on **sustained utilization** — bursty traffic favors APIs
- Hidden costs both ways: migration effort, prompt re-tuning on model swaps, egress
- Do the math with your own traffic — no universal answer

## Distillation: Frontier → Open

### How Capability Flows Downstream

- **Knowledge distillation**: train a smaller student on a stronger teacher's outputs
- Synthetic data generation from frontier models is now a standard training ingredient
- Reasoning distillation: DeepSeek-R1 distilled variants brought chain-of-thought behavior to small open models
- Caveat: most frontier API terms restrict using outputs to train competing models — licenses again
- Result: the open ecosystem trails the frontier by months, not years

## Small Models, Big Roles

### Right-Sizing

- Not every task needs a frontier model
- Small open models (1B–14B) excel at: classification, extraction, routing, drafting
- **Cascade / router patterns**: cheap model first, escalate hard cases to the frontier
- Fine-tuned small model on a narrow task can match a general frontier model at a fraction of the cost

## Strategic Considerations

### Organizational View

- **Portfolio strategy**: frontier API for hard reasoning, open weights for volume and sensitive data
- **Abstraction layer**: route through a gateway so models are swappable
- **Exit planning**: what happens when a provider deprecates your model?
- **Geopolitics and sovereignty**: national/sector rules may mandate on-prem open weights
- Re-evaluate quarterly — this landscape moves fast

## Case Discussion

### You Are the Architect

- Healthcare startup: patient-note summarization under HIPAA — which way and why?
- Consumer app with 50M requests/day of simple classification — which way and why?
- Internal coding agent for a bank's proprietary codebase — which way and why?
- Defend your choice on capability, privacy, cost, and license grounds

## Hands-on Lab

### Comparing Open-Weight and Frontier Models

- Take one task from your project and a small private eval set
- Run it against a frontier API model and a self-served open-weight model (vLLM)
- Compare: quality on your evals, latency, cost per 1K requests
- Write a one-page model-selection recommendation
